Subject: Observability onboarding for Acme Robotics — kickoff & priorities

Hi Marissa / Redwood team,

Thanks again for agreeing to help us onboard observability for the ACME inference pipeline. We're getting the last of our infra in place this week and want to align on a pragmatic first sprint focused on three deliverables:

- Dashboard baseline (overall latency / error / throughput panels for inference routes)
- Tracing hooks (server-side entry/exit spans + span names for request routing)
- Alert lanes + runbook skeleton (what routes alert to on-call vs paging)

Our main risks are noisy alerts from a percent-weirdness metric and under-instrumented batch jobs that bypass the standard trace middleware. Samir (cc'd) owns infra and will be the technical counterpart.

Can we do a 60-minute working kickoff today or tomorrow to draft the mutual action plan and assign owners? If you share a short agenda I can pull the right stakeholders.

Thanks,
Elaine Gardner
Product Ops Manager
Acme Robotics

On Mon, Dec 29, 2025 at 9:13 AM Elaine Gardner <elaine@acmerobotics.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for agreeing to help us onboard observability for the ACME inference pipeline.

Elaine — quick note on what I'll bring to the workshop: a minimal tracing-hook-template (attached) that we've used for GPU-backed routers and for serverless batch jobs. Key points to validate in the meeting:

- Where do requests enter the system (LB / API gateway / direct socket)? We need the canonical entry point to guarantee consistent span IDs.
- For batch jobs, ensure there is a parent span if the job spawns multiple inference shards. If the job runs outside our middleware we'll provide a lightweight mixer to add trace headers.
- Sampling: recommend adaptive sampling by route for the first 2 weeks (1% baseline, 10% on error spikes).
- Span naming: use service.operation.route (e.g. inference.generate.kvcache) — we'll propose a canonical list during the session.

I'll also sketch a dashboard wireframe live (latency P95/P99, token throughput, errors by type, trace waterfall for slow requests).

Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Elaine / team — adding a few practical alert-routing defaults so we can get to a sane baseline quickly:

- Alert lanes (initial):
  * SevP1 (paging): inference_error_rate > 2% sustained for 5m OR 50% increase vs rolling 1h baseline
  * SevP2 (ticket + on-call ack window): latency_p99 > 2s for core-routes OR repeated KV cache misses > threshold
  * SevP3 (do not page): dashboard anomalies / single-route error spikes under configured threshold

- Escalation: page on-call SRE (8x5 primary rotation) for P1, fallback to platform lead if unacked for 15m. We'll provide an alert-lanes-v1.csv you can import to your alerting tooling.
- Runbooks: we'll create a runbook skeleton per SevP1 route with triage checklist, quick mitigation (scale up pool / fallback model), and post-incident action items.

I'll keep the taxonomy intentionally narrow at first (auth errors, infra timeouts, model decode failures, kvcache_miss) and expand after week 1.

Ben Carter
Ops Solutions Lead — Redwood Inference
